title: Emergency Veterinary Case: A Dog with Leishmaniasis and Severe Anemia
description: A dog found in very poor condition with leishmaniasis and severe anemia was immediately taken to a veterinary clinic and received two BHOC administrations to support oxygenation.
heading: Emergency Veterinary Case: A Dog with Leishmaniasis and Severe Anemia
lead: A dog was found on the street in very poor condition and was immediately brought to a veterinary clinic. The case record identifies leishmaniasis and severe anemia. The clinical photographs supplied for this case show the dog first outdoors and subsequently receiving veterinary care in the clinic. The clinic photograph is used as the primary image because it documents the patient in a care setting without making the distressing street photograph the lead visual.

topicSections.title: Emergency presentation
paragraphs: The initial hematology report is dated 10 May 2024. It recorded hemoglobin (HGB) 65, red blood cell count (RBC) 2.78 and hematocrit (HCT) 19.4%. The values are transcribed from the supplied laboratory photograph. Units are not added because they are not clearly legible in the image. The report also records WBC 23.41 and ESR 49; these are retained as source values rather than interpreted as standalone diagnostic findings.

topicSections.title: Two BHOC administrations to support oxygenation
paragraphs: During emergency veterinary care, the dog received BHOC on two occasions to support oxygenation and hemoglobin-based oxygen transport. This is the precise treatment description confirmed for publication: two administrations, with oxygenation support as the stated purpose.

The case material also mentions 120 mL, but it does not establish whether this is the total volume across both administrations or the volume of each administration. For that reason, the article does not assign the 120 mL figure to either interpretation. The treatment record should be consulted before publishing a dose total or per-administration volume.

topicSections.title: Leishmaniosis and hematological findings
paragraphs: Published veterinary guidance describes anemia and changes in the leukogram among possible clinicopathological findings in canine leishmaniosis. The pattern and severity vary between patients, and a complete assessment requires clinical examination and disease-specific testing. A complete blood count is one component of the diagnostic assessment; it does not independently confirm leishmaniosis.

The supplied case record identifies leishmaniasis. This article does not independently re-diagnose the dog or infer disease stage from the photographed blood count. The recorded HGB, RBC and HCT values are presented as the initial laboratory findings, with their units and reference interpretation limited to what can be read in the source.

topicSections.title: The oxygen-transport question
paragraphs: Hemoglobin concentration is relevant to the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity. In a patient with severe anemia, the clinical team must assess the underlying disease and the patient's overall oxygenation and circulation. The clinical question addressed in this case is the support of oxygen transport during emergency veterinary care.

BHOC (Biological Hemoglobin Oxygen Carrier) is being developed within Precision Oxygen Therapeutics. The two administrations recorded here were intended to support oxygenation. This case report documents the intervention; it does not establish that BHOC treats leishmaniasis, demonstrate a causal improvement in clinical outcome, or establish efficacy from a single patient.

topicSections.title: Case documentation
paragraphs: The case is presented as a clinical observation based on the supplied photographs and initial hematology report. No post-treatment laboratory series, follow-up examination, survival outcome or independently adjudicated endpoint has been supplied for this publication. Those details are therefore not inferred.

The purpose of documenting cases in BHOC Veterinary is to describe the clinical setting, the physiological question and the intervention recorded, while distinguishing clinical observations from evidence generated through structured studies. Further evaluation requires defined populations, product characterization, appropriate comparators, safety monitoring and prespecified clinical and functional outcomes.
